Run tests with `env -u CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL -u CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_TOKEN .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov <files>`. No network, no live model call, no billed call. Do not git commit. NEVER print or write any credential. NO regular expressions in new code. No story vocabulary (no Kristin, truck, laptop, drawer, Michelle, passenger seat, memory card) in non-test code. Tests need at least one synthetic second story with different vocabulary besides the real continuity-initiative package. Write the tests FIRST, run them, confirm they fail for the right reason, then implement until they pass. Run ruff check and ruff format on your files at the end. If a test in a file you do not own fails because of your change, do NOT edit that file: say which test and why in your final message. BACKGROUND. The observation contract says which things the narration must show for an action: `ObservationRequest(action, kind, focus)` (storygame/runtime/observation.py) with kind `look`, `open` or `enter`, built in `WorldCapture._set_observation_request` (storygame/runtime/capture.py); `_required_ids` makes EVERY visible item inside a focused container or supporter a required mention; the prompt line `- Show these in your reply: ...` (ItemFactsProvider._section_user_prompt in storygame/runtime/item_facts.py) and the post-turn observation verifier (relations_from_context) both come from that required list. PROBLEM found live. (1) An underside search of a container (the player feels or searches UNDER or BENEATH it) gets kind `look`, so the container's interior contents become mandatory mentions, although the action is about the underside: correct narrations were rejected for not listing the contents. The owner's requirement: on an underside search the only thing that matters is whether something hidden under the object is found; interior contents need not be mentioned. (2) An opening action on a closed container (kind `open`) makes the contents that opening exposes required for the verifier (it judges the post-change world), but the narrator's prompt was never told: the prompt had neither the required line nor any mention of the contents duty, so the narration was rejected for an unstated requirement. DECISIONS (owner): interior contents STAY required for interior inspection, for opening, for a supporter such as a seat, and everywhere else except an underside search. The narrator must be told of the opening duty BEFORE it writes. A model-answer of unknown must never pick the less demanding scope. YOUR TASK A: the underside scope. YOU MAY EDIT ONLY: storygame/runtime/jev_questions.py, storygame/runtime/capture.py, storygame/runtime/observation.py, the NEW file tests/test_observation_under_scope.py, and tests/test_jev_questions.py and tests/test_observation_mode.py ONLY to add tests or to change an assertion that encodes the old behaviour (say which in your final message). Do not touch item_facts.py (another task owns it), the verifier, engine.py, data/, docs/ or the worker. BUILD 1 (jev_questions.py): add `searches_underneath(ask, command, thing_name) -> bool | None`, written exactly like the existing `opens_container` (same `_answer` helper, one `noul` question with instructions and true/false criteria; read it and tests/test_jev_questions.py first). True means the command has the player search, feel, reach or look UNDER, BENEATH or BELOW the named thing. False means the command only looks at, opens, touches, moves, carries, talks about or goes to the thing, or looks inside it. Use plain words at a 12th-grade level, one idea per sentence, like the neighbouring questions. Follow docs/jev-guard-rules.md (read it) for how a question must be written. BUILD 2 (observation.py): a new bounded kind `under`. In `_required_ids`, for a request whose kind is `under`, the required set is only the visible, seen ITEMS whose parent is the focus and whose relation to it is `under` (use the worldkeeper relation query that `ItemFactsProvider._observation_underside_is_exhausted` uses: `world.parent(x) == focus and world.relation(x) == 'under'`); the interior contents are NOT required. They stay in `visible_things` as optional context exactly as today (candidate ids and visibility are unchanged), so the narrator can still name them. Every other kind keeps today's behaviour byte for byte. A hidden under-item is never visible, so it is never required and never shown. BUILD 3 (capture.py, `_set_observation_request`): after the existing `open` decision, when the focus is a container or a supporter, the kind is still `look`, and no seating/boarding step made it `enter`, ask `searches_underneath(adapter, command, world.name(focus_id))`. True gives kind `under`; False or None keeps `look` (unknown must keep the stricter scope). Ask it only in that case: never for an `enter` or `open` request, never when there is no focus, never for a focus that is neither container nor supporter. It is asked once per turn here (before narration), not per attempt, and must go through the same `adapter` the open question uses so budget and guard handling are unchanged. Read how `adapter` is built in `before_turn` and make sure a missing adapter (offline tests, fixed refusal) behaves exactly as the open question does today. TESTS (tests/test_observation_under_scope.py; look at tests/test_observation_mode.py, test_observation_context.py and test_observation_enforcement.py for stubs and helpers; stub `ask` answers by question id, no network): a) real continuity-initiative package, drawer open with its public supplies and the hidden card already taken: an underside command gives kind `under`, `context.required` is empty, the supplies are still in `visible_things`, `relations_from_context` is empty; b) the same command with a stub answering false gives kind `look` and the supplies required (today's behaviour); c) a stub that returns None gives kind `look` (strict); d) an opening command whose open answer is true never asks the underside question (count asks); an `enter` request never asks it; a focus that is not a container or supporter never asks it; e) a supporter focus (the real passenger seat with the laptop on it) with an underside answer true: required empty; with false: laptop required; plain inspect of the seat still requires the laptop; f) an item that is visibly `under` the focus (synthetic story, public, not hidden) IS required on an `under` request, and a hidden one is not shown or required; g) synthetic second story (different names, e.g. an observatory tray and a boat locker) repeating a), b) and f); h) a full engine turn with the enforcing verifier set (see tests/test_observation_enforcement.py) on an underside command whose narration does not mention the interior contents: the turn commits (verifier not called, because there are no relations) and an unrelated item move is still rejected; i) the default path with observation mode off is unchanged. Keep each test short and independent.
